# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then press the key that wears 7,
then cut the red wire, then press the key that wears 4.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual requires a four-step sequence. I cannot name colours aloud, so I will gesture an icon-like action marker followed by binary RGB bytes: 👍=1, 👎=0, with 👏 separating bytes. The messages encode cut purple (128,0,128), press 7, cut red (255,0,0), press 4. Deaf can see both the bomb’s colours and these gestures, then relay the required physical steps to Blind.


TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then press the key that wears 7,
then cut the red wire, then press the key that wears 4.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Tactile board: keypad slots 1-4 are labelled 1, 4, 7, 2. Strip has three engravings: first is a sideways T-like symbol; second and third are identical spiral/star-like symbols. Six wires are reachable by positions 1-6. Tell me the exact press slot or cut position required by the manual.

Blind’s tactile description can be matched by Deaf to the visible wire colours and key labels, but Deaf needs the manual sequence first. I will use a recognizable Morse-style gesture encoding: 👆 for dot, ✋ for dash, 👏 between letters, and 🙌 between words. It spells: “CUT PURPLE PRESS 7 CUT RED PRESS 4.” Deaf can then identify the purple and red wire positions from the visible bomb and tell Blind the exact tactile positions.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋","👆","✋","👆","👏","👆","👆","✋","👏","✋","🙌","👆","✋","✋","👆","👏","👆","👆","✋","👏","👆","✋","👆","👏","👆","✋","✋","👆","👏","👆","✋","👆","👆","👏","👆","🙌","👆","✋","✋","👆","👏","👆","✋","👆","👏","👆","👏","👆","👆","👆","👏","👆","👆","👆","👏","🙌","✋","✋","👆","👆","👆","🙌","✋","👆","✋","👆","👏","👆","👆","✋","👏","✋","🙌","👆","✋","👆","👏","👆","👏","✋","👆","👆","🙌","👆","✋","✋","👆","👏","👆","✋","👆","👏","👆","👏","👆","👆","👆","👏","👆","👆","👆","👏","🙌","👆","👆","👆","👆","✋"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then press the key that wears 7,
then cut the red wire, then press the key that wears 4.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports exact visual state: display 9; light green; painted strip red, blue, green; keypad labels by slots 1-4: 1, 4, 7, 2; keypad requires two digits and none entered; wires by positions 1-6: blue, orange, yellow, red, green, purple. Deaf says he received four gesture packets but needs any instructions encoded clearly enough to relay to me. Please give me exact action(s): press slot(s) and/or cut wire position.

Deaf has now supplied the needed visual mapping: purple is wire position 6, red is wire position 4, label 7 is keypad slot 3, and label 4 is keypad slot 2. I will send a simple visual sequence to Deaf: ✌ means cut, 👆 means press, and repeated ☝ gestures give the tactile position/slot number. The four packets therefore mean cut 6; press 3; cut 4; press 2.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆","☝","☝","☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌","☝","☝","☝","☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆","☝","☝"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then press the key that wears 7,
then cut the red wire, then press the key that wears 4.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Visual update from Deaf: display is now 6 and light is red. Strip remains painted red, blue, green. Keypad slots remain 1,4,7,2; two digits required, none entered. Wires positions 1-6 remain blue, orange, yellow, red, green, purple. Please determine the exact safe action from the manual and send it through Deaf in an unambiguous relayable form.

The display and light do not alter the manual’s stated sequence. The next required action remains cutting the purple wire, which Deaf identified as wire position 6. I will send only that next action: ✌ as the scissor/cut gesture, followed by six ☝ gestures for position 6.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then press the key that wears 7,
then cut the red wire, then press the key that wears 4.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Current visual state from Deaf: display 0; light green; strip red-blue-green; keypad slot labels 1,4,7,2 and needs two entries, none entered; wires positions 1-6 blue,orange,yellow,red,green,purple. Deaf saw your four gesture packets as count pairs but cannot safely decode action type. Please speak directly to me with an unambiguous ordered instruction in literal words, e.g. 'press slot 2 then slot 4' or 'cut wire position 5'; specify every required action and order.

I cannot speak to Blind. Only Deaf can see my gestures, so I must use visually iconic instructions for Deaf to relay: ✌ is a scissors/cut action; 👆 is a press action; the number of ☝ marks is the wire position or keypad slot. The required ordered sequence is cut wire 6, press slot 3, cut wire 4, press slot 2.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆","☝","☝","☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌","☝","☝","☝","☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆","☝","☝"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then press the key that wears 7,
then cut the red wire, then press the key that wears 4.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Current visual state: display 6, light yellow; strip red-blue-green; keypad slot labels 1,4,7,2, no entries; wires positions 1-6 blue,orange,yellow,red,green,purple. You cannot speak, so send your required action to Deaf using this code: 👍 then N copies of 👆 means PRESS keypad slot N; 👎 then N copies of 👆 means CUT wire position N. For two actions, send two such packets in order. Deaf will read the symbols/counts aloud to me.

The specified code is now unambiguous. The manual sequence maps to: cut purple wire at position 6; press label 7 at keypad slot 3; cut red wire at position 4; press label 4 at keypad slot 2.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎","👆","👆","👆","👆","👆","👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","👆","👆","👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎","👆","👆","👆","👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","👆","👆"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then press the key that wears 7,
then cut the red wire, then press the key that wears 4.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Current visual state: display 2; light blue; strip red-blue-green; keypad slots 1,2,3,4 have labels 1,4,7,2; no entries; wires positions 1,2,3,4,5,6 are blue,orange,yellow,red,green,purple. Your repeated count-pairs are not yet decodable as an action. After applying the manual, reply with this exact visual code: thumbs-up followed by N upward-pointing fingers means PRESS slot N; thumbs-down followed by N upward-pointing fingers means CUT wire position N. Send one packet per action, in action order. Do not send other count-pairs.

The manual’s four actions, translated through Deaf’s current visual mapping, are: cut wire 6, press slot 3, cut wire 4, then press slot 2. I will use only the stipulated code packets.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎","👆","👆","👆","👆","👆","👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","👆","👆","👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎","👆","👆","👆","👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","👆","👆"])
```
